note: Enframing (Gestell) reduces entities incl. students/teachers to 'resources' (Bestand) lacking intrinsic meaning, producing an 'ontological drift toward meaninglessness' increasingly obscured by information (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.249, 253-254).

Genuine education 'lays hold of the soul itself' and transforms it by leading the learner to the place of essential being (Wesensort) (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.252-253, quoting Plato's Teaching on Truth p.167).
Contrast term: 'lack of education' (Bildungslosigkeit), a state in which no fundamental comportment is awakened, no measure-giving preconception established (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.256).
Names the contemporary technological 'mode of revealing' that forces entities into a calculative stamp or mould, reducing them to optimizable resources (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.248-249).

Bildung's naming force runs two directions: forming (impressing an unfolding character) and pre-conception (Vor-bild, a measure-giving vision) that antecedently guides the forming (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.255).

Maps Plato's cave onto four pedagogical stages: captivity to shadows/resources, negative freedom (recognizing the fire as enframing), positive freedom/dwelling (ascent to the open), and return to teach (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.256-258).

Cites Heidegger's What Is Called Thinking? claim that teaching is harder than learning because the real teacher lets nothing else be learned than learning; lehren (teaching) as lernen lassen, not belehren (instructing) (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.259-260).

Extends the historical 'essence of truth' doctrine of 'On the Essence of Truth' (1929) into an account of how ontotheological epochs ground the historical development of educational institutions (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.245-248).
Republic Book VII allegory of the cave read as the founding pedagogical text disclosing (and ambiguating) the essence of paideia (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.252-253).
Cites Jaeger's Paideia as the philological source establishing paideia as a key term, while flagging its resonance with Nazi-adjacent vitalist rhetoric (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.253, note 30).

Contests Readings' materialist account (The University in Ruins) of Bildung's obsolescence as reducible to bourgeois economic revolution, arguing Heidegger's ontohistorical account of a dissolving guiding idea is more satisfactory (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.251-252, note 25).

Contests Kripke's rigid-designator conception of essence as inapplicable to Heidegger's verbal, historical sense of Wesen (essence as how beings essence or remain in play) (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.245-246, note 4).
Flags Feenberg's 'Hegelian misinterpretation' of Heidegger's understanding of essence as a targeted counter-reading (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.246, note 6).

Reads enframing as grounded in an 'unthought' Nietzschean ontotheology of beings as eternally recurring will-to-power, the metaphysics underwriting the reduction of beings to resources (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.248-249).
Invokes Derrida's 'phoenix motif' reading of Heidegger's Inaugural Lecture and Derrida's own restaging of it in 'The Principle of Reason' (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.251-252, note 26).
Cites Humboldt's humanist ideal linking 'objective Wissenschaft' to 'subjective Bildung' as the historical unifying strategy Heidegger's re-ontologized education recombines (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.261).
Notes Kerr's satirical label 'Multi-versity' for the internally fragmented, uni-versity-in-name-only that Heidegger's 1929 diagnosis anticipates (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.250-251).

Qualifies the modern, nineteenth-century understanding of Bildung as deliberate cultivation of 'subjective qualities' as a misinterpretation, while preserving the word once its 'original naming power' is restored (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.255).

Insists Heidegger's Destruktion of education has an inseparable positive (recovery) moment alongside its negative (clearing-away) moment, against a polemical reduction of deconstruction to mere destruction (Zerstorung) (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.243-244).

Draws the 1929 Inaugural Lecture's diagnosis that the rootedness of the sciences in their essential ground has dried up and died as evidence of hyper-specialized fragmentation (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.249-251).
Primary text for the recovered 'essence of paideia' and the cave-allegory pedagogy of ontological freedom (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.252-259).
Source of the 'teaching is harder than learning' passage and the definition of learning as bringing what we do into co-respondence with what addresses us as essential (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.259-260).

Illustrates via biology (the logos of the bios) that positive sciences rest on unexamined ontological posits Heidegger's ontological education would teach students to interrogate (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.261-262).

Re-essentializes the empty formal ideal of educational 'excellence' as Aristotelian arete grounded in Dasein's essence as world-disclosure, aiming to reunify teaching/research and the fragmented departments (FAITHFUL-Thomson, p.260-262).
